newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTR-Cons Rutile looks at franking credits.
newsitem.headline: RTR-Cons Rutile looks at franking credits.

text.p: Mineral sands miner Consolidated Rutile Ltd said on Wednesday it was examining ways of releasing A$86.65 million of franking credits in its accounts for the benefit of all shareholders.
"We are examining several options and the board hopes to be in a position soon to make an announcement," Consolidated Rutile chairman, Mark Bethwaite told the annual meeting.

Bethwaite, who is chief executive of RGC Ltd, the controlling shareholder of Cons Rutile's parent Cudgen RZ, also said it was the board's intention to resume paying dividends as soon as uncertainties surrounding CRL's suspended mineral sands project in Sierra Leone, West Africa were resolved.

RGC executive director, finance, Peter Housden who is also a Consolidated Rutile director, told reporters after the meeting that the options for the release of the franking credits included cash-scrip alternatives.
Housden said the company wanted to conserve cash ahead of a restart of the Sierra Leone operations, where CRL had a 50 percent interest, representing an investment of about $90 million.

"Sierra Rutile is widely acknowledged as one of the finest natural rutile deposits in the world with the potential to play a vital role in the economic recovery of Sierra Leone," Bethwaite told shareholders.
RGC acquired a controlling stake in Cudgen through an on-market bid last August and now has 76.7 percent of Cudgen shares, Bethwaite said.
He told Cudgen shareholders that both the company's bentonite operations at Miles in Queensland and interests in a copper-gold exploration joint venture in Irian Jaya in Indonesia had been reviewed.
The company was awaiting final submissions from interested parties who had tendered for the sale of the bentonite asset, he said.

"The board intends to conduct a review of the Irian Jaya exploration venture to determine whether it is in shareholders' best interests to continue funding this activity," Bethwaite said. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
